newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates fall in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates fall in slow trade.

text.p: Croatia's money market rates dropped on Monday morning amid weak kuna demand, dealers said.
"The market has seen very little trade due to the banks' high liquidity. Some of them took out repo loans on Friday to settle their payments," a dealer told Reuters.
Total trade was put at a meagre 4.5 million, leaving a surplus of some 30 million kuna.
Call money fell to 10.5 percent from last week's 11 percent and accounted for one million kuna trade.
One one-month interbank loan was granted at 15 percent.
There was no overnight trade at the weekend thanks to no shortfalls with the banks' balances totalling 473 million.
